main_body: Dark green-brown ground patch (gothic), 64x48 px, a repeating tile pattern of dark moss/stone with small tufts; it is a flat terrain surface, not a standing object
top_band: none - flat terrain patch with no standing top/front structure; column scan shows only repeating ground texture rows (L~50 with periodic L=76 and L=31 stripes)
evidence: Terrain tiles (ground) are not standing objects, so the 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply. The drawing is a flat repeating ground texture with no side faces and no elevation view. Terrain kind matches the content. Nothing here violates the 3/4 contract for a ground patch.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 80 colours and 26 per tile for the grass reference. Paving has 7 colours, but it reads as stone slabs with clear per-stone shading. The candidate is a dark, nearly uniform green with a repeated tufted motif and a few reddish dots. It has about 3 usable lightness steps, with little variation in tone and little grain. The repeating stamp pattern is obvious, with tufts and dark bars in an identical grid, which looks mechanical and not hand-shaded. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are tinted rather than neutral, so the outline is a material tone. Even so, it is clearly thinner than the grass reference in colour count and richness of texture.
